labels.label: ersrem:note_two_ghds_constructed
labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right. The docstring cites the label as `ersrem:note_two_ghds_constructed` (character 698), with no **`...`** mark. Its other bold-backtick items (**`exists_isMaximal`**, **`chrusciel_theorem_2_2`**) carry no prefix:, so tools/ledger.py's mark regex does not read them as marks. I read the Lean against ghd_02_19.tex:731-733 (Remark 3.56), :117 (extendible GHD, MGHD), :115 (GHD = GH with Cauchy surface S) and :560-562 (Thm 3.45's conclusion), and against the extraction eperon2018predictability.txt:1318-1323, which matches. (1) The sentence 'Zorn shows there exists a MGHD which contains Phi_a', and the same for Phi_b, is exists_isMaximalDevelopment: IsExtension U0 u0 U u together with IsMaximalDevelopment. Its added or abstract hypotheses are all disclosed in the checklist (MaximalZorn.lean:83-88), in SCOPE and in REPORT labels[0].hypotheses: the equation abstract (sol, cau with SolutionLocal, SolutionsGlue, CausalityFollows, as in Causal.ErsMughd); GHD read as 'S Cauchy in U for cau u' (OQ-57 (c) is still an OPEN question in registers/DECISIONS.md:213, so the row has to stay partial); M T2; and hanti, antisymmetry of <=_U of cau u on the domain of every solution. (2) IsExtension (U <= U' and EqOn u u' U) is :117's 'M ⊊ M' and u = u' on M' without the strictness. IsMaximalDevelopment says every development extending (U, u) has domain <= U. isMaximalDevelopment_iff proves it equivalent to :117's 'not extendible' (no development with U < U' and EqOn u u' U). Both are faithful under the S-Cauchy reading. (3) 'These two MGHDs are clearly distinct': ers_remark_3_56 concludes x ∈ Ua' ⊓ Ub', ua' x ≠ ub' x and ¬(Ua' = Ub' ∧ EqOn ua' ub' Ua'). Its hypotheses ha, hb, hx, hab are exactly Thm 3.45's conclusion (:561). (4) 'Not maximal' is not formalised. 'Infinitely many' is formalised in its abstract half only: ers_remark_3_56_family turns a family that differs pairwise at a common point into pairwise distinct maximal developments. Both are disclosed. (5) ers_remark_3_56_of_curveNested replaces hanti by hsub, harc and hm, through Causality.antisymm_of_curveNestedOn. These are ers_remark_4_78's hypotheses minus hmacausal, and they are jointly satisfiable: ErsMughd's timelikeLine_ers_theorem_4_79_4_80 discharges hsub and harc on the timelike line. (6) The chain step. isDevelopment_sSup_of_isChain is proved, and ersMor_hypotheses shows that Developments sol cau S : Type (max u v) with ersMor satisfies MorphismsCompose, UniqueMorphisms and ChainsInherit.{max u v}. #check with pp.universes confirms that the size universe is ChainsInherit's first parameter, so v = w. exists_isMaximalDevelopment is indeed derived from AbstractDev.exists_isMaximal_of_chainsInherit (MaximalZorn.lean:961-965), not from a second Zorn. isMaximal_ersMor_iff identifies the abstract IsMaximal with IsMaximalDevelopment. (7) The witness timelikeLine_ers_remark_3_56 (sol U u := U = ⊤, cau const timelikeLine, S = {0}, the constants 0 and 1) discharges every hypothesis of ers_remark_3_56, hanti included (timelikeLine_isCausal). It is degenerate, as disclosed, but it shows the hypothesis set is satisfiable. (8) hanti is disclosed: checklist row :85 ('⚠ named hanti'), SCOPE :93, REPORT hypotheses[2] and questions[2]. Its justification wording is imprecise (finding 2). Binder note: the proposed ett lists Causal.AbstractDev.chrusciel_theorem_2_2, which no Remark 3.56 theorem uses (the remark's existence goes through exists_isMaximal_of_chainsInherit, and rigidity or inextensibility is not part of the remark). It omits Causal.ersMor_hypotheses, the bridge that exists_isMaximalDevelopment does use. This adds no double-DAG edge (AbstractDev uses no other label's declarations); it is the master's choice.

labels.label: Chruściel 1112.5779 Thm 2.2 (not ledgered; Causal.AbstractDev)
labels.notes: Archived statement (references/sbierski/text/chrusciel2013maximal.txt:262-275): 'Theorem 2.2 Let S be a n-dimensional manifold and let (M, g, i) be a Lorentzian (n + 1)-dimensional W-manifold (M, g) with a W–compatible embedding i : S → M. Suppose that the property W is chain-inheriting, and that the only isometry of a W-manifold (M, g) which is the identity on a W-compatible hypersurface is the identity map. (2.1) Then there exists a Lorentzian W-manifold (M̃, g̃, ı̃) with a W-compatible embedding ı̃ : S → M̃ and a C¹ isometric embedding Φ : M → M̃ satisfying ı̃ = Φ ∘ i such that M̃ is inextendible in the class of Lorentzian W-manifolds with a W-compatible embedding of S.' The docstring quote (:18-25) is verbatim, and so are those of :242-246, :355-356 and Remark 2.3.1 (:277-278). Hypothesis by hypothesis for chrusciel_theorem_2_2: (a) the W-manifold (M, g, i) with its embedding is `X : D` in an abstract class with carriers and a morphism predicate. MorphismsCompose renders isometric C¹ embeddings with Φ ∘ ı̃ = ı̃₁ (identity, composition). (b) 'W chain-inheriting' is ChainsInherit.{v}: every non-empty coherent chain of at most v developments has a cocone (IsCocone, the maps p ↦ [p]∼). This is a disclosed reading. It bundles Chruściel's chain inheritance with the 'not too difficult' gluing of (2.2), on chains with chosen compatible maps. Asking it for all coherent chains is no stronger than asking it for chains in MW(M, g, i): restrict to the cofinal part above one member and precompose. (c) (2.1) is RigidEndomorphisms: every endomorphism of a development is the identity. That is weaker than (2.1), which covers any W-compatible hypersurface, and it matches Chruściel's own use at :345-347, where Φ̃₁ ∘ Φ̃ is an isometric self-embedding fixing ı̃(S). (d) Chruściel proves that the collection is a set (Whitney, :291-311). Here that is SizeBound.{v}, a hypothesis, but free at v = w (sizeBound_self). (e) The conclusion '∃ Z f, mor X Z f ∧ IsInextensible mor Z' (every morphism out of Z is an isomorphism) is Chruściel's conclusion. exists_isMaximal is Zorn (exists_maximal_of_chains_bounded) applied to Tower/IsTower: subsets of the v-small R that contain X₀, with a total preorder and unique chosen coherent morphisms. A maximal tower's cocone Z, moved into R, is maximal, because an extension outside the tower would extend the tower (IsTower.extend). It uses no rigidity and no antisymmetry. IsMaximal.isInextensible is Chruściel's :340-347 argument. exists_upperBound_of_uniqueMorphisms and exists_isMaximal_of_uniqueMorphisms are Chruściel's route under unique morphisms (Zorn on the preorder itself, ChainsInherit.{w}), as claimed. exists_isMaximal_of_sequences asks only for bounds on ℕ-sequences of extensions and on chains with no countable cofinal sequence, with no coherence and no rigidity, as claimed. Counterexamples, none vacuous: twoMor_rigid_not_unique has rigid endomorphisms and two morphisms false → true (id and not), so (2.1) does not give uniqueness. ordinalMor_separates (Ordinal.{v} : Type (v+1), ChainsInherit.{v} by Ordinal.bddAbove_of_small, unique morphisms, no maximal element by succ) together with not_sizeBound_ordinalMor shows the size bound is needed. natMor_separates (ℕ, SizeBound.{0}, unique morphisms, no maximal element) shows chain inheritance is needed. allMor_separates (one development with carrier Bool, every map a morphism: SizeBound, ChainsInherit and IsMaximal hold, but the constant map is not an isomorphism) shows rigidity is needed for inextensibility. The joint hypotheses are satisfiable, by ersMor_hypotheses and the witness. Nothing is marked, and Chruściel has no ledger row.

findings.what: The 'infinitely many' finding is true but imprecise, and it goes to the author. :542, :732 and :1096 do assert it, and the paper proves it nowhere. But :542's '(cf section sec:nonuniqueness)' points to an explicit argument for infinitude, at :258: 'we could take it to occur at any point between A and B. This leads to an infinite set of possible solutions, and an infinite set of distinct MGHDs'. The paper itself calls that section heuristic (:224, 'to explain heuristically'). Citing only ':220-222' and calling it 'the heuristic Nambu-Goto discussion' reads as if the reference were silent on infinitude. Also, ':1096 uses it' overstates. :1096 restates the claim, attributing it to Section SecIVP (which constructs two MGHDs), and then argues with two MGHDs only.
findings.fix: Cite :258 as the heuristic that the cross-reference points to ('a heuristic in the Nambu-Goto picture, not a proof'), and say that :1096 restates the claim rather than uses it.

findings.what: The disclosure of hanti says '≤ antisymmetric on each solution's domain (implied by GH in ERS's reading)' and 'in ERS's GH reading it is automatic'. hanti quantifies over every (U, u) with sol U u, but in ERS's reading only GHDs are GH. What ERS's smooth reading does give automatically is antisymmetry on the union of a chain of GHDs: a causal loop is compact, so it lies in one GH member. That is not hanti as stated. For an arbitrary solution's domain only subluminality supplies it, which is ers_remark_3_56_of_curveNested.
findings.fix: Reword: 'for the union of a chain of GHDs it follows in ERS's smooth reading (a causal loop is compact, so it lies in one GH member); for every solution's domain, as hanti asks, from subluminality (ers_remark_3_56_of_curveNested)'.

findings.what: SCOPE states as a fact that in Chruściel's classes the embedding of (2.2) is unique 'by the local rigidity of isometries'. The REPORT (chrusciel_theorem_2_2.findings[1]) says this is 'not checked here'. Prop 2.4's case 3 needs time orientation to be preserved (Remark 2.5), and the morphisms in the class are not stated to preserve it. The claim is plausible but unverified, and SCOPE must be true.
findings.fix: Add '(presumably; not checked here)', as the REPORT says.

findings.what: The comparison leaves out an existing route inside this file's closure. Causality.ers_theorem_4_77 (Causal/NestedCausalities.lean:1084) asks for no acausality and no ambient either: T2, S ⊆ U i, antisymmetry on the union, and hpair. For a chain, hpair is automatic (U i ⊓ U j is a member) and S ⊆ U i holds for developments, so the chain step had a route through it. The same holds for isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_inf (ErsUnions, outside the closure). The new lemma is correct and more general: directed families, no S ⊆ U i. But the kb entry as proposed would hide the existing one from the next session's reuse check.
findings.fix: In the docstring and the kb entry, name ers_theorem_4_77 (hpair trivial on a chain) and state the gain: directed rather than totally ordered families, no S ⊆ U.
